title: The Mirror That Runs Late
text: A merchant in a veil sells mirrors that show a room a moment later than it is. He offers one to a single House, free, and will not say why.

options.label: Hang the late mirror in the hall and watch for what is coming.

outcomes.text: The mirror shows a knife before it is drawn. The House sleeps safer, though it trusts its servants less.
One evening the mirror shows a Scion's chair empty and bloodied. Three days later the chair is empty, its Scion with the surgeon.

options.label: Break it; no House should see what is coming.

outcomes.text: It breaks into seven shards, each still a moment late. You bury them in seven places.
Bad luck is only a saying, people tell the Scion who swung the hammer. They do not believe it either.

options.label: Take it and sell it to a rival; let them see what comes for them.

outcomes.text: A rival pays handsomely. You never ask what it shows them.
